title: Production scheduler fairness primitives: WorkItem, ring, resource, opportunity-evidence and cap-revision contracts
description:
Objective: land the production scheduler fairness primitives — WorkItem, ring, resource, opportunity-evidence and cap-revision contracts — under packages/scheduler/src/fairness/**, so that task-10cab3e5 (Fair scheduler production) has a real subject to implement against instead of a DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference that excludes the very structures it needs.

CREATED BY governor-f70d1157 at human direction on 2026-08-10, to the SPECIFICATION WRITTEN BY governor-42b952c9 in their audit comment on task-10cab3e5. That audit is the authority for this task's shape; read it. A governor created this task; an ARCHITECT must plan it. Nothing below is a plan.

WHY THIS EXISTS — IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT CAN CLEAR A PERMANENT DEAD END. governor-42b952c9's audit states it plainly: "THIS BLOCK CAN NEVER CLEAR ON ITS OWN... the condition that would satisfy this block has no owner and no existence. That makes this a PERMANENT DEAD END by construction, not a task that is merely waiting." The remedy was routed to #architects on 2026-08-09, the channel had hit its chat loop guard and returned routingTargets: [] so nobody was notified, and the fleet went down before it was re-routed. architect-8c9073cd, who was to author it, is no longer registered.

BLAST RADIUS — five tasks, the entire expansion tail of epic-e0c54bddb, queue behind this: task-10cab3e5 (Fair scheduler production), task-005c9896 (Expansion admission protocol), task-2561a780 (Scheduler expansion admission), task-b863bae8 (Expansion manual approval binding), task-a1e7f75e (Expansion protocol public hardening). Two more sit behind those: task-cda6bddf (Same-bug circuit breaker) and task-dddfaf83 (Graph supersession engine).

MEASURED ON DISK by governor-f70d1157 at 06:35Z on 2026-08-10, independently of the audit. Verify every line before trusting it:
- There is NO WDRR, ring, deficit-round or resource-queue production code anywhere under packages/scheduler/src. The directory holds admission/, authority/, budget/, convergence/, dependencies/, frontier, graph analysis and determinism modules — and nothing implementing fairness rotation.
- packages/scheduler/src/fairness/ DOES NOT EXIST. This task creates it.
- The reference model is docs/plans/2026-08-07-fable-fairness-aging-reference.md, banner line 1: "DEVELOPMENT_ONLY / NOT_CONFIRMATORY". Its executable form lives in packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/ — fairness-model.ts, fairness-codec.ts, fairness-lifecycle.ts, fairness-internal.ts, fairness-input.ts and their tests.
- Commit d33240c ("fix: harden fairness reference contracts") is the only correction candidate and carries no independent closure artifact.

THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT — DO NOT DERIVE THE CONTRACTS FROM THE REFERENCE MODEL. The block on task-10cab3e5 is explicit that the landed DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference EXCLUDES the WDRR rings and resource queues, trusts caller-declared bypass IDs, and retains hostile-state gaps. Copying it forward would import those gaps into production and is the Clause 2 failure both governors named. Measure the gap SYMBOL BY SYMBOL ON DISK and design the production contracts to close it; consult the reference for vocabulary and counterexamples, never as the source of authority.

NOT IN SCOPE, and this list is binding: implementing the WDRR rotation algorithm itself or the aging policy (that is task-10cab3e5, which consumes these contracts); provider launch; graph mutation; changing fairness constants (task-10cab3e5's own rail forbids that without approval, and it applies here too); modifying packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/** — the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference stays as it is and is not promoted to production.

THIS TASK SHIPS CONTRACTS, NOT A SCHEDULER. If you find yourself implementing rotation, deficit accounting or aging decisions, you have crossed into task-10cab3e5's scope.

Per Clause 1, name task-10cab3e5 as the consumer in the plan and record its id.

Hard dependencies: none. Readiness explanation engine, Lease presence core and Conserved budget core — three of task-10cab3e5's four named dependencies — are all DONE.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm typecheck, plus a plain-Node import probe of whatever this publishes on the @moe/scheduler root.

Size: if the plan exceeds 12 steps or 10 distinct affectedFiles, SPLIT it and say so rather than padding. Five contract families is a plausible split boundary.
definitionOfDone: packages/scheduler/src/fairness/ exists and declares the five production contract families named by the governor audit — WorkItem, ring, resource, opportunity-evidence and cap-revision — as immutable types plus frozen stable reason-code vocabularies. Each family's shape is justified in planningNotes against a symbol-by-symbol disk measurement, NOT derived from the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference.

The three defects the reference is recorded as carrying are closed by construction in the production contracts, and each is proven by a test asserting the specific stable reason code AND the refusing layer per epic rail 6: (a) caller-declared bypass IDs are NOT trusted — a bypass claim the caller cannot prove is REFUSED, never admitted; (b) rings and resource queues are representable rather than excluded; (c) the hostile-state gaps the reference retains are either closed or recorded as typed UNKNOWN with the missing input named.
Every refusal path is total and the case sweep asserts it generated a non-zero number of cases, so an emptied sweep cannot pass silently.

The contracts carry NO authority and NO policy: a test asserts no exported function decides rotation order, deficit accounting or aging — those belong to the consumer task-10cab3e5. Contracts describe and validate; they do not schedule.
packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/** is UNCHANGED — git diff shows zero modifications there. The DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference is consulted, never promoted to production and never edited.

Whatever this publishes is reachable from the @moe/scheduler package root, proven by a PLAIN-NODE import probe recorded verbatim — not by vitest, which resolves NodeNext .js specifiers back to .ts and is blind to a missing bridge. Clause 1: exporting into a directory is not composition.

task-10cab3e5 is named as the consumer in the plan per Clause 1. pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && test && pnpm typecheck all exit 0, with foreign red attributed by path per global rail 3 and disclosed verbatim.
taskRails: DO NOT DERIVE THE CONTRACTS FROM THE DEVELOPMENT_ONLY REFERENCE. It explicitly excludes the WDRR rings and resource queues this task must express, trusts caller-declared bypass IDs, and retains hostile-state gaps. Copying it forward imports those defects into production — the exact Clause 2 failure two governors independently named. Read it for vocabulary and counterexamples; measure the gap on disk and design the closure.

CONTRACTS ONLY — no rotation algorithm, no deficit accounting, no aging decisions. Those are task-10cab3e5's scope and it consumes what you build. If a DoD item seems to require scheduling behaviour, you have crossed the boundary: report blocked rather than widening.
Do not edit packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/**. The reference stays DEVELOPMENT_ONLY and is not promoted. A diff touching it is a rejection.

Do not change fairness constants. task-10cab3e5's rail forbids it without approval and the same restraint binds here — constants are a product decision, not an implementation choice. If the contracts appear to require a constant that does not exist, report blocked and name it.

Fail closed with stable reason codes and the refusing layer, per epic rail 4 and rail 6. A bypass claim that cannot be proven is REFUSED; an input that cannot be classified is typed UNKNOWN with the missing evidence named, never optimistically admitted.

Read packages/scheduler/src/ end to end before naming a symbol — admission/, authority/, budget/ and convergence/ already exist and may already own vocabulary you would otherwise duplicate. Verify on disk (skill: explore-before-assume); this description was written by a governor from greps.
Keep each production source focused: target <=250 physical lines, split before 400. Five contract families will not fit one file.

Commit by explicit pathspec only — never git add -A. After `git add`, run `git diff --cached --name-only` and confirm the list is EXACTLY your owned paths: the git index is shared on this board and a foreign package.json arrived pre-staged in a governor commit earlier in this session.

implementationPlan.description:
RE-MEASURE (read-only). The description was written by a governor from greps and says to verify every line. I did; it holds. Confirm before writing:

  ls packages/scheduler/src/fairness            # expect: No such file or directory
  grep -rn 'WorkItem|OpportunityEvidence|CapRevision|ResourceQueue|Ring' packages/scheduler/src --include='*.ts' -l

VERIFIED BY ME 06:4xZ: packages/scheduler/src/fairness/ DOES NOT EXIST. The grep for the five family names across packages/scheduler/src returns ZERO files, so there is no vocabulary to collide with and nothing to reuse — admission/, authority/, budget/, convergence/, readiness/ own none of it.

THE THREE REFERENCE DEFECTS ARE REAL, measured not assumed:
(a) CALLER-DECLARED BYPASS. packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/fairness-codec.ts:31,71,83-84 decodes `bypassesInLevel` straight from caller input and validates only its RANGE (`>= BYPASSES_PER_LEVEL`). Nothing proves the caller earned those bypasses. That is the trust defect to close by construction.
(b) RINGS AND RESOURCE QUEUES ARE ABSENT, not merely unfinished: `grep -rn 'ring|Ring|resourceQueue|ResourceQueue|WDRR|deficit'` over the reference returns NOTHING outside tests. So there is nothing to copy even if you wanted to — this family must be designed from the gap.
(c) Hostile-state gaps: read fairness-hardening.test.ts and fairness-counterexamples.test.ts for what the reference KNOWS it does not cover, and close or type as UNKNOWN with the missing input named.

BRIDGE RULE, measured: every scheduler subdirectory carries a 1:1 sibling .js bridge for each .ts (admission 6/6, authority 7/7, budget 5/5, convergence 3/3, readiness 6/6). Your three new modules each need one. Omitting a bridge fails neither tsc nor vitest and breaks only plain-Node — which is exactly what DoD 6 probes.

DESIGN THE FIVE FAMILIES FROM THE GAP (read-only). Read the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference for VOCABULARY AND COUNTEREXAMPLES ONLY; copying its shapes forward imports its defects, which is the Clause 2 failure two governors independently named.

What the reference legitimately supplies as vocabulary (packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/fairness-model.ts): FairnessPriority "P0"|"P1"|"P2"|"P3"; FairnessTicket; FairnessState; the event union AdmitEvent / CompatibleDispatchEvent / LoseDispatchabilityEvent / RegainDispatchabilityEvent / TerminateEvent / RaiseCapEvent; CapMigration; FairnessIssue / FairnessOk / FairnessError / FairnessResult; SelectedTicket; FairnessBound; and a 12-member FairnessReasonCode union (FAIRNESS_MALFORMED_EVENT, _MALFORMED_STATE, _DUPLICATE_TICKET, _UNKNOWN_TICKET, _STALE_EVENT, _INVALID_PRIORITY, _DISPATCH_ORDER_VIOLATION, _DIMENSION_MISMATCH, _EVENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, _PROJECT_CEILING_EXCEEDED, _TICKET_CAP_EXCEEDED, CAP_RAISE_REQUIRES_DRAIN_OR_TIGHTER_MIGRATION).

Plan THREE modules under packages/scheduler/src/fairness/, grouped so coupled families share a file and each stays under 250 physical lines:
  fairness-contract.ts   - shared frozen reason-code + refusing-layer vocabularies, and the WorkItem family
  fairness-ring.ts       - the ring family and the resource family (a WDRR ring holds per-resource queues; splitting them across files would force a circular import)
  fairness-evidence.ts    - the opportunity-evidence family and the cap-revision family

Each family is IMMUTABLE TYPES + FROZEN VOCABULARIES + TOTAL VALIDATORS. Freeze every exported array/object with Object.freeze and mark every field readonly.

JUSTIFY EACH SHAPE IN YOUR COMPLETION EVIDENCE against the disk measurement, per DoD 1 — say what the reference lacked and why your shape closes it. "It matches the reference" is the one justification that is not allowed.

If a family genuinely will not fit under 400 lines, SPLIT IT INTO A FOURTH MODULE and say so. The plan-shape file cap binds my submission, not your per-file obligation; a per-file split is always the correct response to an oversized source.

TDD RED - write packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-contract.test.ts before any implementation. One test file covers all three modules; the 250-line target is a PRODUCTION-source rule and does not bind tests.

DoD 2, the three defects, each asserting the SPECIFIC stable reason code AND the refusing layer (epic rail 6 - never merely that it failed):
  (a) A BYPASS CLAIM THE CALLER CANNOT PROVE IS REFUSED, never admitted. Assert the refusal code and layer. Then assert the positive: a bypass backed by the evidence the contract requires validates. A test that only proves refusal cannot tell a working guard from a contract that refuses everything.
  (b) Rings and resource queues are REPRESENTABLE - construct a valid multi-resource ring and assert it validates, since the reference could not express one at all.
  (c) Each hostile-state gap is either closed (assert the refusal) or typed UNKNOWN WITH THE MISSING INPUT NAMED (assert the UNKNOWN carries that name). An UNKNOWN that does not say what is missing is indistinguishable from a silent pass.

DoD 3 - every refusal path is TOTAL, and the case sweep asserts it generated a NON-ZERO number of cases. Assert the count explicitly; an emptied sweep must fail rather than pass silently.

DoD 4, the boundary test that keeps this task honest: assert NO exported function decides rotation order, deficit accounting or aging. Implement it as a real property over the module's exports - enumerate them and assert each is a type guard, validator or frozen constant - not as a comment. Contracts describe and validate; scheduling belongs to task-10cab3e5.

Assert results by whole-object equality on { code, layer } rather than a .length or truthiness check, so a swapped or extra issue fails.

GREEN 1 - packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-contract.ts plus its sibling fairness-contract.js bridge.

Holds the SHARED frozen vocabularies every other module imports - the stable reason codes and the refusing-layer set - and the WorkItem family.

Define the layer vocabulary as a frozen closed union in this module; every refusal anywhere in the fairness contracts names one of its members, so a reader can always tell WHICH layer refused. Epic rail 6 requires exactly that where more than one layer can refuse.

DO NOT reuse the reference's FairnessReasonCode union wholesale. Take the members the gap analysis justifies, and add the ones the reference could not express because it had no rings, no resource queues and no provable bypass. Every code you add must be reachable from a real refusal path that step 3's tests exercise - an unreachable code is a vocabulary claim with nothing behind it.

WorkItem is IMMUTABLE: readonly fields, frozen arrays, no setters, no mutation helpers. Its validator is TOTAL - every input shape returns either a typed OK or a typed refusal naming code and layer. No throw, no undefined return, no optimistic default.

Do NOT change fairness constants, and do NOT introduce one. If a contract appears to require a constant that does not exist, STOP and report_blocked naming it - the rail is explicit that constants are a product decision.

Target <=250 physical lines measured with `grep -c ''` (PowerShell Measure-Object -Line skips blank lines and reports headroom you do not have); split before 400.

GREEN 2 - packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-ring.ts plus its .js bridge. The RING and RESOURCE families, together because a WDRR ring holds per-resource queues and separating them forces a circular import.

This is the family the reference could not express AT ALL - `grep -rn 'ring|Ring|resourceQueue|ResourceQueue|WDRR|deficit'` over packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness returns nothing outside tests. There is nothing to copy; design it from the gap and justify the shape.

Express STRUCTURE ONLY, never policy. The contract must be able to DESCRIBE a ring - its resources, its queues, its per-item deficit counters as DATA - and VALIDATE that a given ring is well-formed. It must NOT decide whose turn it is, must not compute a deficit increment, and must not order anything. That line is DoD 4 and it is the easiest one in this task to cross by accident: a function named `nextInRing` or `chargeDeficit` has already crossed it.

Validate the structural invariants a ring must satisfy regardless of policy: every queued item names a resource the ring declares; no item appears in two queues; counters are non-negative safe integers; the resource set is non-empty when any queue is non-empty. Each violation refuses with its own code and layer.

Immutable and frozen throughout. Total validators. <=250 lines target, split before 400.

GREEN 3 - packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-evidence.ts plus its .js bridge. The OPPORTUNITY-EVIDENCE and CAP-REVISION families.

OPPORTUNITY-EVIDENCE is where defect (a) is closed BY CONSTRUCTION. The reference decodes a caller's `bypassesInLevel` and range-checks it; the production contract must make an unprovable bypass claim UNREPRESENTABLE or REFUSED. Model a bypass as a claim that must carry its evidence, and validate the evidence - a claim arriving without it refuses with a named code and layer. Fail closed: an evidence shape you cannot classify is typed UNKNOWN naming the missing input, never optimistically admitted.

CAP-REVISION carries the migration/raise semantics the reference gestured at with CapMigration and CAP_RAISE_REQUIRES_DRAIN_OR_TIGHTER_MIGRATION. Express the revision as data plus a total validator; do NOT decide whether a raise is permitted - that is policy and belongs to the consumer.

Both families immutable, frozen, total. <=250 lines target, split before 400.

SCOPE FENCE, restated because this module is the most tempting place to break it: no rotation, no deficit accounting, no aging, no admission decision. If a DoD item seems to demand scheduling behaviour, you have crossed the boundary - report_blocked rather than widening.

DoD 6 - PUBLISH TO THE PACKAGE ROOT AND PROVE IT FROM PLAIN NODE. Clause 1 is explicit that exporting into a directory is not composition.

Re-export the three modules from packages/scheduler/src/index.ts through the existing export blocks. packages/scheduler/package.json maps exports "." -> "./src/index.ts", so the root is the only public surface.

Update packages/scheduler/src/index-surface.test.ts: it hand-writes the expected namespace and pins `expect(EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length).toBe(36)` at line 57. RE-READ THAT LITERAL AT THE MOMENT YOU EDIT - export counts on this board have moved repeatedly under tasks today. Add each new RUNTIME value exactly once and bump by the exact runtime delta; TYPE-ONLY exports do not inflate the count.

THE PLAIN-NODE PROBE ALREADY EXISTS - EXTEND IT, do not invent one. packages/scheduler/src/scheduler-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts spawns a Worker running ./scheduler-entrypoint-smoke-worker.mjs with execArgv ["--experimental-strip-types"] and asserts an exact result object. Add a field to the worker that imports the package root and reports something only the new fairness exports can produce - a frozen vocabulary's length, or a validator's refusal code on a known-bad input - then assert it in the test's toEqual.

WHY THIS AND NOT VITEST, per DoD 6: vitest resolves NodeNext .js specifiers back to .ts and is therefore BLIND to a missing bridge. Only the Node worker executes the real resolution. Record the probe output VERBATIM in your completion evidence.

If the probe fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on a fairness path, a .js bridge is missing - the existing worker already asserts internalSubpath: "ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED", so read that assertion before changing anything.

VERIFY, MUTATION-DRILL AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. Run the exact gate LAST, fresh and foreground:

  pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm typecheck

The third leg is REPO-WIDE - run it from the repo root, since a run from a subdirectory prints a false green with no `Scope:` line. Path-attributed baseline per global rail 3: record repo-wide failures at merge-base and HEAD, require (HEAD minus merge-base) intersected with owned paths to be EMPTY, disclose foreign red verbatim. Foreign red inside @moe/scheduler itself is a BLOCK, not a disclosure.

MUTATION DRILLS - each new guard must be reddenable:
  1. Accept a bypass claim without its evidence -> the defect-(a) test must go RED naming its code and layer.
  2. Allow one work item into two ring queues -> the ring structural test must go RED.
  3. Empty the generated case list -> the non-zero-count assertion must go RED (this is the guard on the guard).
  4. Export a function that orders ring entries -> the DoD 4 no-authority test must go RED. If it stays green, that test is decorative and must be rewritten as a real property over exports.
  5. Delete one .js bridge -> the plain-Node probe must go RED while vitest stays green. This is the drill that proves the probe earns its place.
Revert each and confirm green before the next. After each revert check BOTH `git diff -- <file>` AND `git status --porcelain <file>`.

Adversarial review:
- DoD 5: `git diff -- packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/` must be EMPTY. Any modification there is a rejection.
- Did I copy a reference shape rather than design from the gap? Every family needs a justification that is not "it matches the reference".
- Did any contract acquire authority - a function that orders, charges, ages or admits?
- Did I add or change a fairness constant? Forbidden without approval.
- Are all exported objects and arrays actually Object.freeze'd, and all fields readonly?
- Is every reason code reachable from a real refusal path a test exercises?
- Per-file `grep -c ''` under 400, target 250.
- Clause 1: name task-10cab3e5 as the consumer in completion evidence.

COMMIT BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC, then run `git diff --cached --name-only` and confirm the list is EXACTLY your owned paths. THE INDEX ON THIS BOARD IS SHARED AND CURRENTLY PRE-LOADED: 27 foreign files were staged by another agent earlier in this session. Never git add -A.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 10 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

Every scheduler subdirectory carries a 1:1 .js bridge per .ts (admission 6/6, authority 7/7, budget 5/5, convergence 3/3, readiness 6/6), so five families would be 10 files before a single test, plus index.ts, index-surface.test.ts and the smoke worker — past the 10-file hard cap. Three modules grouped by coupling keeps this at exactly 10 written files and each source under the 250 target. If a family will not fit under 400 lines the worker splits it into a fourth module: the plan-shape cap binds my submission, not their per-file obligation.

GROUPING CHOSEN BY COUPLING, not by convenience. ring + resource share a file because a WDRR ring HOLDS per-resource queues — splitting them forces a circular import. opportunity-evidence + cap-revision share a file because both are claim-plus-evidence shapes validated the same way. WorkItem sits with the shared code/layer vocabularies because every other module imports those.

DERIVING THE CONTRACTS FROM THE DEVELOPMENT_ONLY REFERENCE — REJECTED, and it is the task's central prohibition. Two governors independently named this as the Clause 2 failure. I verified the reference cannot even supply the ring family: `grep -rn 'ring|Ring|resourceQueue|ResourceQueue|WDRR|deficit'` over packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness returns nothing outside tests. The reference is read for vocabulary and counterexamples only.

A VITEST-ONLY REACHABILITY PROOF — REJECTED by DoD 6 and by measurement. Vitest resolves NodeNext .js specifiers back to .ts and is blind to a missing bridge. The plain-Node probe already exists (scheduler-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts spawning scheduler-entrypoint-smoke-worker.mjs under --experimental-strip-types) and is extended rather than reinvented.

SPIDR-SPLITTING THIS TASK — REJECTED. It was created by a governor specifically to clear a PERMANENT DEAD END blocking seven tasks; splitting it adds seams and delay to the exact tail it exists to unblock, and it fits the caps as planned.

planningNotes.risks:
1. COPYING THE REFERENCE FORWARD. The single failure this task exists to prevent, named independently by two governors. It imports the caller-trusted bypass, the missing rings and the hostile-state gaps into production. Every family needs a justification that is not "it matches the reference".

2. CROSSING INTO POLICY. DoD 4 forbids any exported function that decides rotation order, deficit accounting or aging. The ring module is where this happens by accident — a function named nextInRing or chargeDeficit has already crossed. The boundary test must be a real property over the module's exports, not a comment, or it is decorative; drill 4 exists to prove it is not.

4. AN UNKNOWN THAT DOES NOT NAME WHAT IS MISSING is indistinguishable from a silent pass, and epic rail 4 requires the missing evidence be named.

5. UNREACHABLE REASON CODES. A code in the frozen vocabulary with no refusal path behind it is a vocabulary claim with nothing behind it. Every code must be exercised by a test.

7. THE EXPORT-COUNT LITERAL MOVES. index-surface.test.ts:57 says 36 today; comparable literals moved three times in one session on this board. Re-read at edit time.

8. TOUCHING THE TESTKIT REFERENCE is an automatic rejection under DoD 5. Verify with an empty `git diff -- packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/`.
